hypothesis: FP16-accumulate P.V in the prefill kernel _attn_fwd (both the unmasked causal loop and the masked loop): compute each tile's P.V as tl.dot(p.to(fp16), v.to(fp16), out_dtype=fp16), i.e. mma.sync m16n8k16 f16.f16.f16.f16, then fold it into the fp32 accumulator with one fused rescale-add acc = acc*alpha + pv.to(fp32). Q.K^T, softmax stats (m_i, l_i) and the running accumulator stay fp32. Decode/split kernels unchanged.
rationale: Large prefill is at the fp32-accumulate tensor ceiling: prefill_32768 = 8.8 TFLOP causal in 39.4 ms = 223 TFLOPS. On GeForce Blackwell (as on Ada), mma with FP32 accumulate runs at half the FP16-accumulate rate (5090 spec: 419 dense FP16-acc vs 209.5 FP32-acc). FA2 uses fp32 accumulate everywhere, so it is capped at the same ceiling. Moving the P.V half of the FLOPs to f16 accumulate halves its tensor time. Accuracy: p in [0,1] is rounded to fp16 (10-bit mantissa) instead of bf16 (7-bit), which is more precise than today. bf16->fp16 for V is exact in the normal range. The fp16 rounding applies only within one BLOCK_N tile (K=32..128), and partial sums are added to fp32, so per-row error should stay below bf16 output rounding. Never tried: exps 3-6 tuned tiles and order but all kept fp32 mma. Costs: a bf16->fp16 cvt per V element and an f16->f32 cvt per accumulator element per tile. Both are ALU/MUFU-free work that should overlap with the tensor pipe.
expected_effect: Prefill rows get faster, most on the compute-bound 8k-32k rows (prefill_32768 is the thinnest prefill margin at 1.03x). The ideal is up to ~25% less tensor time. Realistically 5-15% if the cvts overlap and Triton still pipelines the V loads through smem. Decode is untouched. Risk: if Triton converts V before the shared-memory stage and breaks cp.async pipelining, prefill could regress.
